set.title: EDA software market: segments, vendors, concentration and China's domestic EDA
set.why_it_matters: Every chip is designed with EDA software. The market is small (ESD Alliance counts about US$5.5bn a quarter including IP) but three US-headquartered vendors dominate and the US has used EDA as an export-control lever, so EDA is a chokepoint out of proportion to its revenue.
questions: How does ESD Alliance split design-industry revenue (CAE, IC physical design and verification, PCB/MCM, SIP, services) and how big is each category?
What are Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA's shares of EDA revenue, and how do they differ by tool category (synthesis, place-and-route, sign-off, verification, analog/custom)?
Which design steps have a single dominant tool, and which have credible alternatives?
How large and capable are Chinese EDA vendors (Empyrean, Primarius, Semitronix, X-Epic) and what share of China's demand do they serve?
How did the Synopsys-Ansys merger and its competition remedies change the market structure?
What is the geographic split of EDA revenue by customer region?
subquestions: Does ESD Alliance data include IP, and how does that affect 'EDA market' figures quoted by others?
Which tools are certified in foundry reference flows for the leading nodes (TSMC N2/A16, Samsung SF2, Intel 18A)?
What did the May-July 2025 US EDA licence requirement for China reveal about dependency?
primary_sources: ESD Alliance Electronic Design Market Data (EDMD) quarterly releases
Synopsys and Cadence Form 10-K (revenue by product group and geography)
Siemens AG annual report (Digital Industries Software segment)
Empyrean Technology (SZSE 301269) and Primarius (SSE STAR 688206) annual reports (to verify tickers)
FTC / EU Commission / SAMR decisions on Synopsys-Ansys merger (2025)
BIS Federal Register rule on ECAD for GAAFET (Aug 2022) and 2025 BIS letters to EDA vendors (to verify)
secondary_sources: CSET 'The Semiconductor Supply Chain' (2021) EDA share estimates
Jon Peddie / TechInsights EDA analyses (to verify)
open_questions: Seat and bundle pricing is not public (INT-0009); money side sits in RU-0024 and a business-model unit.

set.title: Back-end stage map: assembly and test market, OSAT vs in-house vs foundry, leaders and geography
set.why_it_matters: Every chip must be cut, packaged and tested, and at least 81% of that capacity is in Asia. The back end is measured inconsistently (OSAT revenue, IDM in-house work, TSMC's Foundry 2.0 counting) so nobody can say cleanly how large it is, who does what share, or which countries hold it.
questions: How large is the outsourced assembly and test (OSAT) market and what are the top-10 OSAT shares on a consistent year?
What share of assembly and test is done in-house by IDMs and memory makers vs outsourced, and how has it changed since 2015?
Where is back-end capacity by country (China, Taiwan, Malaysia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore, South Korea, Japan, US, Mexico, Portugal/Europe, India)?
How is 'advanced packaging' defined by different publishers, and how large is it vs conventional (wire-bond, leadframe) packaging?
Which new back-end plants are being built (India ATMP projects, US Amkor Arizona, Vietnam, Malaysia expansion) and with what subsidies?
How does TSMC's 'Foundry 2.0' definition shift packaging and test revenue across category lines?
subquestions: Which OSATs are owned by or tied to chip companies (e.g. JCET and SMIC links, ASE's EMS arm USI)?
Which package types dominate by unit volume vs by value?
Which association member lists enumerate OSATs by country (MSIA Malaysia, SEIPI Philippines, TSIA Taiwan, CSIA China, SEMI)?
primary_sources: ASE Technology Holding annual report and Form 20-F
Amkor Technology Form 10-K (revenue by package type and plant location)
JCET, Tongfu, Huatian annual reports (SSE/SZSE)
Powertech Technology annual report (TWSE)
TSMC annual report and quarterly management report (Foundry 2.0 definition)
India Semiconductor Mission approved ATMP/OSAT project list (MeitY/ISM)
US CHIPS Program Office award announcements (Amkor Arizona)
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) E&E statistics; SEIPI Philippines export data (to verify)
SIA/BCG 'Emerging Resilience in the Semiconductor Supply Chain' (2024)
secondary_sources: Yole Group OSAT and advanced packaging market releases
open_questions: Foundry vs OSAT split of advanced packaging is unknown (CLM-0539); RU-0036 covers the advanced side.
Pricing is in RU-0022 and INT-0008, not here.

set.why_it_matters: Displays, solar PV, LEDs, passive components, PCBs and EMS share equipment, materials, factories, classification codes or sales channels with semiconductors but are excluded from 'the semiconductor market'. Without explicit boundaries, market sizes get double-counted and supplier dependencies (e.g. polysilicon, equipment makers' display business) get missed.
questions: Which adjacent industries share process equipment, materials or fabs with semiconductors (flat-panel displays, solar PV, LEDs/micro-LED, MEMS foundries, hard-disk heads)?
Which are inside vs outside WSTS, SEMI, NAICS 3344 and HS 8541/8542 definitions (e.g. solar cells in HS 8541, LEDs as optoelectronics)?
How large is each adjacent industry and how much do semiconductor suppliers (AMAT display, Canon/Nikon FPD lithography, polysilicon makers) depend on it?
Where do passive components, connectors and PCBs share distribution channels and shortage cycles with chips?
What scope decisions should the atlas record, and why?
subquestions: How much solar-grade vs semiconductor-grade polysilicon does each producer make?
Are LEDs and image sensors counted as optoelectronics in WSTS?
primary_sources: WSTS product classification definitions
US Census NAICS 2022 manual (3344 subsectors)
WCO HS 2022 nomenclature notes to Chapter 85 (8541/8542)
Applied Materials 10-K (Display and Adjacent Markets segment)
Canon and Nikon annual reports (FPD lithography)
Wacker Chemie annual report (Polysilicon segment, semiconductor vs solar split)
IEA PV reports / IEA 'Solar PV Global Supply Chains' (2022)
IPC / Prismark PCB market data (to verify)
open_questions: Overlaps RU-0009 (official classifications): this unit decides scope; RU-0009 maps codes.

set.title: Advanced packaging technology and capacity: 2.5D interposers (CoWoS-class), fan-out, 3D stacking and hybrid bonding
set.why_it_matters: AI accelerators cannot be built without 2.5D/3D packaging, and in 2023-2025 packaging capacity (not wafer capacity) limited AI chip supply. A few firms (TSMC first) hold the know-how and capacity, and the foundry-OSAT boundary is moving.
questions: What are the main advanced-packaging platforms (silicon-interposer 2.5D, RDL/bridge 2.5D, fan-out, SoIC/Foveros 3D, hybrid bonding, panel-level) and which firm offers each?
What is CoWoS-class capacity (wafers per month) by provider and year, and how fast is it expanding (TSMC, ASE/SPIL, Amkor, Intel, Samsung)?
What split of advanced-packaging work goes to foundries vs OSATs, and how is the work divided on one package (e.g. chip-on-wafer at foundry, substrate attach at OSAT)?
What are the capacity bottlenecks (interposers, substrates, HBM, hybrid bonders, TCB tools) and their lead times?
Which equipment is specific to advanced packaging and who supplies it (BESI, ASMPT, Hanmi, Disco, EVG, AMAT, Tokyo Electron)?
Where is advanced packaging capacity being built outside Taiwan (US NAPMP-funded, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, India)?
subquestions: How is 'advanced packaging' revenue counted by TSMC, Yole and SEMI respectively?
What yields and cycle times are disclosed for 2.5D packaging?
primary_sources: TSMC annual report and earnings call transcripts (CoWoS/SoIC capacity statements)
ASE, Amkor, Intel annual reports / 10-K
BESI, ASMPT, Disco, Hanmi annual reports (hybrid bonding and TCB orders)
NIST CHIPS National Advanced Packaging Manufacturing Program (NAPMP) vision paper and NOFOs
IPC 'North American Advanced Packaging Ecosystem Gap Assessment' (2021)
IEEE Heterogeneous Integration Roadmap (HIR)
open_questions: HBM stacking itself is split into a new HBM manufacturing unit; substrates into the IC-substrates unit.

set.title: Lithography tools and the EUV subsystem supply base: ASML, Zeiss, Cymer/Trumpf, Nikon/Canon, High-NA adoption
set.why_it_matters: Every leading-edge chip needs EUV scanners from one company, ASML, which itself depends on single suppliers for optics (Zeiss), light sources and lasers. This is the clearest single-supplier chokepoint in the industry.
questions: What are lithography system unit shipments and revenue by technology (EUV, ArF immersion, ArF dry, KrF, i-line) and vendor (ASML, Nikon, Canon, SMEE)?
Which subsystems of an EUV scanner have a single source (Zeiss optics, Cymer source, Trumpf CO2 drive laser, VDL modules) and what are their capacities?
How many EUV and High-NA EUV systems are installed and ordered, by customer region?
How many EUV layers do leading logic and DRAM processes use, and how is High-NA being adopted (Intel 14A, TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix)?
What alternatives exist (nanoimprint at Canon, DUV multipatterning in China, SMEE, electron-beam direct write)?
How did the lithography market concentrate historically (Nikon/Canon share loss after 2000)?
subquestions: What is ASML's shipment split by country (China share) and how did controls change it?
primary_sources: ASML annual report and Form 20-F (system sales by technology and region)
Carl Zeiss AG annual report (Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology segment)
Nikon and Canon annual reports (semiconductor lithography unit shipments)
TRUMPF annual report (EUV laser)
imec and Intel disclosures on High-NA
IRDS Lithography chapter
open_questions: Photoresists moved to new unit on lithography materials; masks to the mask-making unit; export-control rules stay in RU-0013/RU-0025/RU-0029.

set.title: Materials segment map: SEMI fab and packaging materials categories, sizes, supplier concentration and production geography
set.why_it_matters: Fabs consume about US$73bn a year of wafers, gases, chemicals, resists, targets, slurries and packaging materials. SIA/BCG flag several as chokepoints, but the segment sizes, leading suppliers per segment and where they are produced have not been mapped on one consistent basis.
questions: What are SEMI's fab-materials and packaging-materials categories and their sizes by year (2019-2025)?
What are materials revenues by region of consumption (Taiwan, China, Korea, Japan, North America, Europe, Rest of World)?
For each category, who are the top suppliers and what is their combined share, and where do they produce?
Which categories are most geographically concentrated in production (Japan in resists, wafers; Korea/Japan/US in gases)?
How are materials bought (spot vs long-term contracts, consignment, vendor-managed inventory)?
Which registries or association lists can enumerate materials suppliers by category (SEMI member directory, JEITA, KSIA, CSIA)?
subquestions: How do SEMI category boundaries compare with company segment reporting (e.g. Entegris, Merck Electronics, Resonac)?
primary_sources: SEMI Materials Market Data Subscription (MMDS) public press releases
Entegris 10-K, Merck KGaA annual report (Electronics), Resonac, Shin-Etsu, JSR, Sumitomo Chemical annual reports
Japan METI 'Semiconductor and Digital Industry Strategy' documents
European Commission Chips Act staff working document SWD(2022)147 (supply chain analysis)
SIA/BCG 'Strengthening the Global Semiconductor Supply Chain in an Uncertain Era' (2021) and 'Emerging Resilience' (2024)

Segment deep dives: wafers, gases/wet chemicals, litho materials, other consumables, IC substrates, critical minerals (new units).

set.title: Equipment segment map: SEMI segments, sizes, billings by region, leading vendors per tool category
set.why_it_matters: Equipment is a US$135bn market with more than 50 tool types, several of which have one or two credible suppliers. The segment sizes, the leader in each tool category and where the tools are sold are the base for chokepoint and export-control analysis.
questions: What are SEMI's equipment segments (wafer processing, fab facilities, mask/reticle, test, assembly and packaging) and their sizes 2015-2025?
What are equipment billings by region (China, Taiwan, Korea, North America, Japan, Europe, RoW) and how did China's share move after 2022?
Who leads each tool category (lithography, deposition CVD/PVD/ALD, etch, clean, CMP, ion implant, process control/metrology, thermal, test, assembly) and with what share?
How big is the refurbished/used equipment market and who serves it?
What are SEAJ's Japanese-made equipment statistics and what share of global supply does Japan hold?
How is equipment demand concentrated by customer (top customers' share of AMAT, Lam, TEL, KLA revenue)?
subquestions: How do SEMI billings (by customer location) differ from vendor revenue by region?
Which Chinese equipment makers (Naura, AMEC, Piotech, ACM Research, SMEE, Hwatsing) lead in which categories?
primary_sources: SEMI Worldwide Semiconductor Equipment Market Statistics (WWSEMS) press releases
SEAJ Japan-made semiconductor equipment statistics
Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA Form 10-K; Tokyo Electron, Screen, Kokusai annual reports; ASML 20-F
Naura (SZSE 002371), AMEC (SSE 688012) annual reports
CSET/ETO Supply Chain Explorer (chipexplorer.eto.tech) tool-category market shares
secondary_sources: TechInsights / The Information Network equipment share estimates
open_questions: Service/upgrade economics are in RU-0021; sub-tier suppliers in new unit 'Equipment sub-tier supply base'; lithography in RU-0037.

set.title: Distribution channel structure: authorized distributors, brokers, e-commerce catalogue houses and the direct vs distribution split
set.why_it_matters: Distributors sit between chipmakers and tens of thousands of OEM and EMS buyers, and the open-market broker channel is where counterfeits enter. The share of chips sold through each channel is unknown, so we cannot say how much of the industry depends on distributors.
questions: What share of chip revenue goes through distribution vs direct, overall and by chip company (TI, Microchip, ADI, NXP, Infineon, STMicro, Renesas)?
Who are the largest authorized distributors (Arrow, Avnet, WPG, WT Microelectronics, Future, TTI, Digi-Key, Mouser) and their semiconductor revenue by region?
How is Asia's distribution structured differently (Taiwan/HK/China distributors, WPG, WT, Supreme)?
How large is the independent/broker (open) market and the obsolescence aftermarket?
How is counterfeit risk managed (SAE AS6081/AS5553, GIDEP, DFARS 252.246-7007/7008)?
Which lists enumerate distributors (ECIA members, ERAI, GSA)?
subquestions: How did TI's shift to direct sales change the channel?
primary_sources: Arrow and Avnet Form 10-K; WPG and WT Microelectronics annual reports (TWSE)
Chip-company 10-K/20-F disclosures of distributor share of revenue (TI, Microchip, ADI, NXP, ON Semi)
US GAO reports on counterfeit parts (e.g. GAO-12-375)
DFARS 252.246-7007/7008 and SAE AS6081/AS5553 standards
ECIA industry data and member list
secondary_sources: Supply & Demand Chain Executive / EE Times distribution coverage
open_questions: Margins, price protection and ship-and-debit are in RU-0019 (INT-0007); share of direct vs distribution is CLM-0570 / INT-0018.

set.title: Fab-support services: parts cleaning and coating, wafer reclaim and test wafers, used-equipment brokers and spare parts
set.why_it_matters: Beneath fabs sits a layer of small specialist firms that clean and recoat chamber parts, reclaim test wafers and trade used tools. They are rarely counted in market figures but a fab cannot run without them, and many are single-region.
questions: Who provides chamber-part cleaning, coating and refurbishment (UCT/QuantumClean, Pentagon Technologies, Frontken, KoMiCo, Mitsubishi Chemical cleaning) and where?
How large is the reclaim and test/monitor wafer market and who serves it (RS Technologies, Phoenix Silicon, Kinik)?
How large is the used and refurbished tool market, who brokers it, and how important is it for 200mm and mature-node fabs (including China)?
How do fabs source spare parts (OEM vs third-party) and what are typical lead times?
Which of these services are geographically concentrated or depend on one supplier per fab?
subquestions: Do export controls apply to used tools and parts sold into China?
primary_sources: Ultra Clean Holdings Form 10-K (services segment)
Frontken (Bursa Malaysia) and RS Technologies (TSE) annual reports
SEMI secondary equipment and applications (SEMI Secondary Equipment Special Interest Group) materials (to verify)
BIS EAR provisions on used equipment and parts (15 CFR 744.23)
open_questions: Logistics and fab construction were split into their own new units.
